clue.text: Forbearance exhibited by VP getting a titanium implant

indicators.note: the vice president is getting an implant, so the other letters go inside his name

parts.note: Mike Pence was US Vice President when the puzzle appeared
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium

explanation.surface: A US vice president undergoing surgery for a titanium implant shows great forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like medical news, but 'implant' is part of the insertion signal: the VP's surname is opened up to take the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance and patience are synonyms: both mean calm tolerance of delay or provocation.

clue.text: Prepared case, having got verbal agreement

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word for agreement is said out loud

parts.note: a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A lawyer readied a case after striking a spoken agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal agreement' looks like a single phrase, an oral deal, but 'verbal' is the sound signal. The answer also ties to the theme song: Nellie packed her trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase that has been filled and readied for a trip is packed, so the participle fits the phrase.

clue.text: On which 24 28 had a moonlit rendezvous in the Burmese way?

definitions.text: On which 24 28 had a moonlit rendezvous in the Burmese way?

parts.words: On which 24 28 had a moonlit rendezvous in the Burmese way?
parts.note: in the theme song the elephant meets the herd one night in the silver light on a route to a city in Burma, which is the Burmese way

explanation.surface: A question about where the elephant of 24 and 28 met her herd by moonlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The song lyric runs 'they met one night in the silver light on the road to Mandalay'. Mandalay is a city in Burma (Myanmar), and the phrase is also a Kipling poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a route to a Burmese city, literally a Burmese way, where the song's meeting took place.

clue.text: English conservationists, doubly green, railed about Anglo/French agreement

indicators.note: doubly says the first two pieces appear twice over

parts.note: the National Trust, NT, is the British heritage conservation charity
eco is the prefix for environmentally green

indicators.note: about signals the letters of railed being moved around

explanation.surface: Doubly green English conservationists rail against a pact between Britain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' applies to the English conservationists, not to green. The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and landscapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 understanding between Britain and France is known by this French phrase meaning friendly understanding.

clue.text: One in jail caught Señora Peron climbing quietly inside

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the soft letter goes inside the reversed name
in a down entry, climbing means the name is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president, was known as Evita
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A jailbird caught Eva Perón quietly climbing into the prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses EVITA to ATIVE in this down clue, and 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive is a prisoner, someone held in confinement such as a jail.

clue.text: One gets off to a flying start participating in three sets

definitions.text: One gets off to a flying start

indicators.note: the answer is only participating in that string, so the spare letters at either end are dropped to leave the run inside it

parts.note: three sets written out in full gives the word set three times in a row

explanation.surface: A tennis player gets off to a flying start in a three-set match.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect hidden word: 'three sets' must first be written as SETSETSET, and 'participating in' then finds the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This African insect is a fly, so the whole word 'flying' is where its name starts: it is literally a flier from the outset.

clue.text: I brush pagans off nonchalantly, being a man of God

indicators.note: nonchalantly suggests the letters of the words are tossed about casually

explanation.surface: A clergyman casually waves away the heathens around him.
explanation.definitionFit: This churchman is an assistant bishop serving under a diocesan bishop, so he is a cleric, a servant of God.

clue.text: Chest beginning to throb, jog back in last place

indicators.note: beginning to takes the start of the word throb

parts.note: to jog is to run at a gentle pace

indicators.note: in last place takes the final letter of the word back

explanation.surface: A jogger's chest starts to throb and the runner drops back to last place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the word whose end is taken, not a reversal signal. The answer fits the theme: Nellie packed her trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk is a large storage box, the same thing as a chest.

clue.text: Manhattan district steadies corruption

indicators.note: corruption implies the word steadies has its letters debased into another order

explanation.surface: A Manhattan neighbourhood keeps corruption in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan's Upper and Lower East Side are well-known areas of the island, named for their location by the East River.

clue.text: Swiss psychiatrist left base in tropical forest

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A Swiss psychiatrist abandons his base for the rainforest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but gives L; 'base' is e, the mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: A jungle is dense tangled forest typical of hot, wet regions near the equator.

clue.text: Salesman in court moved cautiously

indicators.note: the salesman is placed in the court, inside its letters

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman in a courtroom tiptoes about warily.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and stealthily; the past tense matches 'moved'.

clue.text: Spurs' foul new sports kit

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of these words are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur's new kit is foul, a fan complains.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club; 'new' rearranges SPURS and FOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: These baggy trousers gathered below the knee were traditional golfing wear, so they are a piece of sporting clothing.

clue.text: Speaking clearly, deploring departing daughter

indicators.note: the daughter is departing, so her letter leaves the word

parts.note: denouncing something is publicly deploring it

explanation.surface: Someone loudly condemns a daughter who is leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or articulate words distinctly, a formal word for clear utterance.

clue.text: Sir Francis's day off? Works in the garden

indicators.note: the day is off, taken away from the name

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan sea captain; his name with the possessive gives the letters

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake spends his day off pottering in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the verb sense: a gardener who rakes is drawing a toothed tool over soil or leaves, a typical garden job.

clue.text: Dread her egg sandwiches? Show faith!

indicators.note: the words dread her egg sandwich the answer between their outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone who dreads her egg sandwiches is urged to keep faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food from the surface's egg, but it is the verb signalling letters held within.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause or belief is to stay loyal to it, which is showing faith in it.

clue.text: Working, as one intended?

definitions.meaning: a machine's gears that are ... are in operation, busy at work
an intended is a fiancé, and someone with an intended is betrothed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both occupied or in action, and promised in marriage, the state of a person with an intended.

clue.text: Having set sail, catch large bird circumnavigating America

indicators.note: the bird is circumnavigating, sailing right round, the word for catch

parts.note: a goose is a large waterbird
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off to catch a big seabird on a voyage round America.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has gone to sea has embarked on a voyage, which matches having set sail.

clue.text: See 2
In the mood for love, alpha male old Proust undressed

parts.note: alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A

indicators.note: undressed strips off the outer letters of the novelist's name

explanation.surface: An alpha male seduces the elderly novelist Proust, who is undressed and in the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means feeling romantic or sexual desire, a mood for love.

clue.text: Skinny bairn regularly chucked in the naughty corner?

indicators.note: regularly chucked means every second letter of skinny bairn is thrown away

explanation.surface: A thin Scottish child keeps getting sent to the naughty corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairn is the Scottish word for a child. A sin bin is where sports players are sent for a spell after a foul; the question mark flags the stretch to a nursery corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are places of temporary banishment for misbehaviour, whether for a child or a sports player.

clue.text: Doggy's stick to carry home

definitions.note: read as doggy is, so an adjective meaning dog-like

indicators.note: the stick is to carry the other piece inside it

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means at home

explanation.surface: A dog has a stick it carries home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'Doggy's' means 'Doggy is', giving an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is the adjective for anything relating to or resembling dogs.

clue.text: Senior officer: Ewell must be evacuated

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a colon

indicators.note: Ewell must be evacuated, emptied of its inner letters, leaving its outside pair

explanation.surface: A senior officer orders that the town of Ewell be evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own punctuation is used: the colon gives COLON. Ewell is a town in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a high-ranking army officer, above a major and below a brigadier.

clue.text: Split involving George — gutless as he was — in 1815

indicators.note: the tear is involving, wrapping around, the other letters

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

indicators.note: gutless removes the inside of George, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rift arises involving a cowardly George, as he was in 1815.
explanation.walkthrough: The future George IV was Prince Regent from 1811 to 1820, ruling for his ill father George III, so in 1815 that was his title.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who cannot, which was George's role during 1815.

clue.text: Lawrence, boring old man, rather passé

indicators.note: the initials are boring into the father, drilling inside him

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, a dad
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: Lawrence finds the boring old man rather out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like an adjective for the old man but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated has gone out of fashion, which is what passé means.

clue.text: Weekend golfer partial to sweet rum punch

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weekend golfer has a fondness for sweet rum punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Trump, US president in 2020, was famous for spending weekends at his golf courses.
explanation.definitionFit: The president was well known for golfing at weekends at his own resorts, so the description identifies him.

clue.text: She received a trunk call from outside The Circus

definitions.text: She received a trunk call from outside The Circus

parts.words: She received a trunk call from outside The Circus
parts.note: in the children's song the ... packs her trunk and leaves the circus when the herd calls her from far away; a trunk call is also an old long-distance phone call

explanation.surface: A woman takes a long-distance phone call from somewhere outside a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: The British children's song has the line 'packed her trunk and said goodbye to the circus'; she answers the call of the herd. A trunk call was the British term for a long-distance phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine is called by her herd, the trunk-trumpeted call, from beyond the circus where she worked.

clue.text: Praise Austrian driver into flying

parts.note: Niki Lauda was the Austrian Formula One world champion

indicators.note: flying sends the letters of into flying about

explanation.surface: An Austrian racing driver deserves praise for getting into flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Lauda founded airlines after racing, so 'flying' fits his life but signals the rearrangement of INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudation is a formal word for commendation or high praise.

clue.text: Speed, heroin & ecstasy going round varsity every now and again

indicators.note: the two drug letters are going round the picked letters, enclosing them

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: every now and again takes every other letter of the word varsity

explanation.surface: Speed, heroin and ecstasy are doing the rounds at university now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and again' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of varsity, AST. Speed is also a drug, so the definition hides among the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste means hurry or quickness, so it is a synonym of speed in the sense of rapid action.

clue.text: Year One's protective equipment here finally, hooray!

parts.note: One is the Roman numeral I, and its possession follows
PPE stands for personal protective equipment

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of here

explanation.surface: A Year One pupil's protective gear has finally arrived, to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 2020, when PPE, personal protective equipment, was in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of delight or celebration.
